balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Seagate Technology Holdings plc: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Seagate Technology Holdings plc: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Seagate Technology Holdings plc: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Seagate Technology Holdings plc: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Seagate Technology Holdings plc: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

hddShipments.title: HDD exabytes shipped and price per TB
hddShipments.content:
Exabytes shipped is the total capacity of hard drives sold in the period; price per TB is the implied average selling price Seagate realises per terabyte of that capacity.

For Seagate: this is the AI-driven data-center demand thesis in two numbers. Hyperscale and enterprise customers are buying ever more nearline (high-capacity, cloud/enterprise) drives to store data generated and consumed by AI training and inference, and Seagate's HAMR-based Mozaic drives are the newest, highest-capacity point in that line-up. Volume growing while price per TB holds or rises -- rather than volume growth funded by price cuts -- is what a durable, not merely cyclical, upswing looks like.

What to watch:

  • Exabytes shipped growing faster than revenue (price erosion) or slower (price-led growth)
  • Nearline mix within total exabytes -- the higher-capacity, higher-margin product driving the AI buildout
  • Price per TB holding through a volume ramp, since HDD cycles have historically punished oversupply with sharp price cuts

marketMix.title: Revenue mix by end market
marketMix.content:
Seagate splits revenue (and HDD exabytes shipped) by end market. From FY2026 it reports Data center (nearline/mass-capacity drives and systems sold to cloud and enterprise customers) versus Edge IoT (consumer/client, NAS, mission-critical and SSD). FY2023-FY2025 periods use the retired Mass Capacity / Legacy / Other split -- a different grouping of the same underlying business, not a comparable trend line.

For Seagate: the shift to a Data center/Edge IoT presentation itself signals how concentrated the business has become in AI-adjacent cloud storage -- Data center was already roughly three-quarters of revenue when the new split was introduced and has kept climbing.

What to watch:

  • Data center share continuing to rise as the AI storage buildout continues
  • Edge IoT (the more consumer-cyclical, lower-growth remainder) shrinking as a share of the total
  • Don't read FY2023-FY2025 and FY2026-on series as one continuous line -- the category definitions changed

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Seagate Technology Holdings plc: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Seagate Technology Holdings plc: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Seagate Technology Holdings plc: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Seagate Technology Holdings plc: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Seagate Technology Holdings plc: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
